description: Verifies horizon-regular spacetimes and horizon handling: Painleve-Gullstrand and Eddington-Finkelstein metrics and connections stay regular from 0.1 to 10 Schwarzschild radii, a free-falling particle and an ingoing photon cross the horizon with preserved invariants, absorption and continuity boundary modes behave as configured, and rays inside the horizon cannot escape.

checks.label: Painleve-Gullstrand: the Schwarzschild radius equals 2 M in geometric units
Painleve-Gullstrand: the inverse metric reproduces the identity at every sampled radius
Painleve-Gullstrand: the analytic and numerical connections are finite at every sampled radius
Painleve-Gullstrand: the analytic connection matches eighth-order finite differences relative to the largest symbol of its row
Eddington-Finkelstein: the Schwarzschild radius equals 2 M in geometric units
Eddington-Finkelstein: the inverse metric reproduces the identity at every sampled radius
Eddington-Finkelstein: the analytic and numerical connections are finite at every sampled radius
Eddington-Finkelstein: the analytic connection matches eighth-order finite differences relative to the largest symbol of its row
every adaptive step of the free fall succeeds
the state stays finite throughout the fall
the particle crosses the Schwarzschild radius
the integrator statistics report the horizon crossing
the particle reaches the deep interior
the temporal velocity of a free fall from rest stays equal to 1
the four-velocity normalization stays equal to -c^2
every adaptive step of the photon succeeds
the photon crosses the Schwarzschild radius
the integrator statistics report the horizon crossing
the photon reaches the deep interior
the advanced time of an ingoing null ray stays constant
the advanced-time velocity of an ingoing null ray stays zero
the radial velocity of an ingoing null ray stays equal to -1
the null constraint holds along the ray
the absorbing integration terminates within the step budget
absorption mode reports the crossing and the absorption
absorption mode does not reach the singularity
the absorbed particle ends at or inside the horizon
the continuing integration terminates within the step budget
continuity mode crosses the horizon without absorption
continuity mode reaches the singularity threshold
the particle ends inside the singularity threshold
the initial radial velocity inside the horizon points inward
every adaptive step inside the horizon succeeds
the radius never exceeds the horizon while inside the trapped region
the ray reaches the singularity threshold
